research_rationale:
EO:11696 (signed 1973-01-17; 38 FR 1722, Federal Register of January 18, 1973) excuses Federal employees in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area from duty for one-half day on "Friday, January 19, 1973" (section 1), lets agency heads keep employees at their posts for national security or other public reasons (section 2), and makes that half day a holiday for pay and leave purposes (section 3). Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing in jobs/fr-originals; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: I confirm the dossier's three scopes, sections 1, 2 and 3, as the complete operative text. Each section operates only on that one half day, so all three end by their own terms on 1973-01-19, recorded inclusive (through the end of that day). Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all complete, none with a coverage warning): the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, citations of the order by number in statute text and notes; edition current through 2026-10-09) recorded 0 hits; the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML recorded 0 hits; the Federal Register catalog disposition-note search (1937 onward) recorded 0 hits for this order. I also searched every held order text (the Cruden held-text search, 33118 readable files) for the order's number; the only held texts that cite it are its own Federal Register printing. I found no held order that revokes or amends it.
